decisions.reason: Zimmermann and Lange (2022) designed Experiment 1 (N=6) to replicate the context dependency of perisaccadic displacement suppression reported by Zimmermann (2020, 10.7554/elife.49700, shipped row 2268) before testing contrast suppression in Experiment 2. In a 2x2 repeated-measures ANOVA on Experiment 1 displacement discrimination with factors stimulus time (baseline vs. perisaccadic) and session type (no context vs. context), the authors cite both Bridgeman, Hendry, and Stark (1975) and Zimmermann (2020) for the perisaccadic decline in displacement detection (stimulus time main effect F(1,5)=18.85, p=0.007) and Zimmermann (2020) for the session-type main effect and interaction. The complete primary XML of Zimmermann (2020) confirms that Zimmermann (2020) Experiment 1 already directly measured and statistically confirmed baseline perisaccadic vs. pre-saccadic displacement suppression in no-context sessions (t(3)=-9.38, p=0.0026, d=1.7, citing Bridgeman et al., 1975) alongside context sessions (t(3)=3.68, p=0.017) in the same experimental paradigm. Under the codebook closest-in-chain rule, Zimmermann (2020) is the immediate study in the empirical chain encompassing both the baseline perisaccadic displacement suppression and its context modulation, so the ancestral source Bridgeman et al. (1975) is not an omitted independent target.
